counterfactual.change: Reduced G from 5 to 0.5 (one field), weakening close-encounter acceleration so fixed-dt leapfrog with limited substeps stays accurate; same 3 steps now pass.

explanation: Two 20-mass bodies with G=5 and dt=1/30 fall from 1.58 to 0.56 separation (softening 0.3 scale) in 0.1 time units. Adaptive substeps (14-20 per step) are insufficient for the strong, rapidly varying acceleration, so leapfrog gains ~108 energy vs ~101 allowed, violating energy_conserved. Lowering G removes the stiff close encounter and the failure disappears.
vision_note: Two blue bodies start slightly separated and drift toward each other through steps 0 to 2. By step 3 they have fallen together to near-overlap, showing a rapid close encounter.
